gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the same overstatement: unconditional barycenter convergence is claimed, while the formal result gives convergence to a fixed point and identifies it with the barycenter only under fixed-point uniqueness.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The unconditional computational convergence claim exceeds the conditional theorem because uniqueness of the fixed point of G is not established for general non-parametric inputs.

component_coverage.gold_component: Unconditional convergence to the Wasserstein barycenter is advertised although the theorem only gives barycenter convergence under uniqueness of the fixed point of G.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes unconditional fixed-point accumulation from conditional identification with the barycenter and proposes the same qualification.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The prediction concerns uniqueness needed to identify fixed points with the barycenter. Gold concerns a separate domain hypothesis: bounded density is needed to place the barycenter in P_{2,ac} and justify the G-operator theorem for arbitrary absolutely continuous inputs.

The prediction addresses fixed-point uniqueness and convergence claims, whereas gold concerns insufficient boundary smoothness for the claimed high-order Caffarelli regularity and its propagated consequences.

The prediction identifies non-Borel threshold choices as a source of failed adaptedness, but does not recognize the separate gold obligations to prove Borel measurability of truncation and pushforward operations or to establish the full adaptive construction. Thus it does not cover the full gold concern.

The prediction identifies a missing uniqueness qualification in the mathematical convergence claim. Gold instead concerns the unqualified transfer from an exact-optimization theorem to finite-tolerance Sinkhorn implementations; it requires distinguishing exact theoretical iterates from numerical stopping error.
